title: Registration control flow: Wire -> RegisterAPIService/RegisterAppInstaller -> apiserver/background service
answers: How does a new API builder get installed into the apiserver?
How does an App-SDK app get started at boot?
What calls RegisterAPIService and where does that lead?
body:
API builder path: pkg/server/wire_core.go & pkg/server/bootstrap/wire/sets.go pull in apiregistry.WireSet (pkg/registry/apis/wireset.go) via Wire DI → Wire invokes e.g. folders.RegisterAPIService (pkg/registry/apis/folders/register.go) → builds *FolderAPIBuilder and calls apiregistration.RegisterAPI(builder), where apiregistration is builder.APIRegistrar (pkg/services/apiserver/builder/common.go) → hands the builder to pkg/services/apiserver to install as a real k8s API group. Every builder must satisfy builder.APIGroupBuilder (InstallSchema, UpdateAPIGroupInfo, GetOpenAPIDefinitions, AllowedV0Alpha1Resources).
App path: appregistry.ProvideAppInstallers (pkg/registry/apps/apps.go) collects installers from e.g. playlist.RegisterAppInstaller (pkg/registry/apps/playlist/register.go) → returns []appsdkapiserver.AppInstaller → appregistry.Service.Run (pkg/registry/apps/apps.go) drives runner.APIGroupRunner.Init/Run, itself a registry.BackgroundService.
Final fan-in: backgroundsvcs.ProvideBackgroundServiceRegistry (pkg/registry/backgroundsvcs/background_services.go) depends on *apiregistry.Service and *appregistry.Service as forced-init sinks, folding both into the single list pkg/server iterates to call Run(ctx) on at boot.
